Boole: 1 - H(z_B) <= sum_k P(|Z_k| > z_B) = K x 2(1 - Phi(z_B)) = K x alpha/K = alpha, so H(z_B) >= 1 - alpha and h <= z_B. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html lines 596-600 (equicorrelated normals are MTP2 for 0 <= rho < 1; their one-sided p-values are MTP2; Simes inequality; Theorem 7.5), Lab 5 hypothesis (line 638)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 202ea24 (git diff checked); round-11 evidence: Re-derived and re-tested at 45559ab, independently of this row's earlier evidence: see L05-math-card-c180 (sympy inverse, the sign argument, 4,000 random pairs per rho, negative control, Simes event probabilities for the 450 true nulls). unchanged since 3dd9a69 (git diff checked); round-9 evidence: Re-derived and re-checked from scratch at 3dd9a69. The only changes in this paragraph since 7cdab4c are the range '\rho \ge 0' -> '0 \le \rho \lt 1' (sentence 1) and '\rho \ge 0' -> '\rho \in [0, 1)' (last sentence), plus the grade markup (see L05-grade-mtp2); the derivation is unchanged. (i) Sigma = (1-rho) I + rho 11' has inverse (1/(1-rho)) (I - (rho/(1-rho+m0 rho)) 11'): multiplying out, (1-rho) I + 11' (rho - (rho/(1-rho+m0 rho))(1-rho+m0 rho)) = (1-rho) I, so Sigma^-1 Sigma = I; off-diagonal entries are -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m0 rho)) <= 0 for 0 <= rho < 1, exactly the page's formula. Numerically equal to np.linalg.inv for rho in {0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95} and m0 in {2, 5, 50, 450} (tolerance 1e-9). (ii) For u = x v y and v = x ^ y the diagonal terms cancel because u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2, leaving log f(u) + log f(v) - log f(x) - log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j): maximum absolute error 3.6e-12 over 32,000 random pairs (rho in {0, 0.3, 0.8, 0.99}, m in {2, 3, 6, 20}; scripts/mtp2_check.py). (iii) The bracket is 0 when x_i - y_i and x_j - y_j have the same sign (then {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i} and {u_j, v_j} = {x_j, y_j} in the same order, so u_i u_j + v_i v_j = x_i x_j + y_i y_j) and (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise (x_i >= y_i, x_j <= y_j gives u_i u_j + v_i v_j = x_i y_j + y_i x_j); both cases asserted on every random pair. With Q_ij <= 0 every term is >= 0, so f(u) f(v) >= f(x) f(y); the smallest observed value of the combination was -2.3e-13 (rounding). (iv) p = 1 - Phi(z) is decreasing in each coordinate, so it swaps v and ^ (h(x v y) = h(x) ^ h(y)); the Jacobian is a product of one-coordinate factors and {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i} makes it equal at (u, v) and (x, y); hence the p-values are MTP2. (v) MTP2 implies the Simes inequality: I opened Lehmann and Romano (2005), arXiv math/0507420v1 (the Annals of Statistics 33(3) 1138-1154 text; Crossref: 10.1214/009053605000000084): Theorem 3.2(ii) states 'if the joint distribution of the p-values of the true null hypotheses satisfies Simes inequality ... then P{FDP > gamma} <= alpha', and the paragraph after its proof says 'Sarkar and Chang [11] and Sarkar [10] have shown that the Simes inequality holds for the family of distributions which is characterized by the multivariate positive of order 2 condition' (Sarkar 1998, Ann. Statist. 26(2) 494-504, doi 10.1214/aos/1028144846; Crossref abstract: an analytical proof of the Simes conjecture for MTP2 random vectors). Assumptions are now complete: at rho = 1 the covariance is singular and (1-rho) = 0 in the inverse, so the density argument does not apply and the page now excludes it; at 0 <= rho < 1 every step holds (m0 = 1 is trivial). Monte Carlo check of the end claim (200,000 draws per cell, one-sided z-tests, the Simes event P(union over l of {q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}) at alpha = 0.05): rho 0: 0.0497 / 0.0491 / 0.0503 for m0 = 5 / 50 / 450 (SE 0.0005); rho 0.3: 0.0475 / 0.0432 / 0.0386; rho 0.5: 0.0443 / 0.0338 / 0.0253; rho 0.8: 0.0354 / 0.0215 / 0.0162; rho 0.95: 0.0329 / 0.0258 / 0.0242; rho 0.999: 0.0466 / 0.0436 / 0.0437; none exceeds 0.05 beyond Monte Carlo error. The fix is the one round 8 proposed.

Dividing every constant of (3) by c = c(floor(gamma m) + 1) is (3) at alpha' = alpha/c (linear in alpha). Theorem 7.5 at level alpha' gives P(FDP > gamma) <= P(U_{l<=M} {q_(l) <= l alpha'/m0}). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Proposition 7.8 and proof (lines 600-607)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 202ea24 (git diff checked); round-11 evidence: no round-9 change was recorded for this row (it carried the round-8 evidence below). round-8 evidence: Re-derived after the rename A -> D. If the original procedure makes no false rejection, the augmented procedure rejects R = R0 + D' with D' = min(D, m - R0) <= D, at most D' of them false; R = 0 gives FDP = 0; otherwise FDP <= D'/(R0 + D') <= D/(R0 + D) because x -> x/(R0 + x) is increasing; and D <= gamma R0/(1 - gamma) iff D (1 - gamma) <= gamma R0 iff D <= gamma (R0 + D), so FDP <= gamma. Hence {FDP > gamma} needs a false rejection by the original procedure: probability <= alpha. Correct, and the letters D, D' no longer clash with the active set A.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 202ea24 (git diff checked); round-11 evidence: Re-derived at 45559ab (the passage around (c) changed). For d_t = phi d_{t-1} + e_t with iid e of variance s^2: the marginal variance is s^2/(1-phi^2); the long-run variance (sum of autocovariances, gamma_h = phi^|h| s^2/(1-phi^2)) is s^2/(1-phi)^2, so T Var(dbar) -> s^2/(1-phi)^2. The iid-studentized t = dbar/(sd/sqrt(T)) therefore has limiting variance [s^2/(1-phi)^2] / [s^2/(1-phi^2)] = (1+phi)/(1-phi) = 1.857 at phi = 0.3 (sd 1.363), as E2(a) and the line-878 bullet say. A single-date bootstrap resamples as if iid, so t* is approximately N(0,1) and its 95% quantile is about 1.645; the test rejects when t > 1.645, with probability P(N(0, 1.857) > 1.645) = 0.1137 (E2(b)). Longer blocks restore the serial dependence in t*, so t* inherits the variance 1.857 and the critical value rises: 0.113 / 0.063 / 0.067 in the snippet (exact rerun), 0.11 / 0.05 / 0.09 in my independent loop version (L05-num-E2). The bullet's claim that the stationary bootstrap 'reproduces the same distortion in t*' is the same fact; nothing in it changed.

rows.location: S7-c180 and L05.html line 596: equicorrelated normals are MTP2 for 0 <= rho < 1; one-sided p-values MTP2; Simes inequality; Theorem 7.5
rows.evidence: unchanged since 202ea24 (git diff checked); round-11 evidence: Re-derived by hand and numerically at 45559ab (scripts/mtp2.py, sympy 1.14, scipy, numpy). (1) Sigma = (1-rho)I + rho 11^T of order m has Sigma^-1 = (1/(1-rho))[I - rho/(1-rho+m rho) 11^T] (Sherman-Morrison), so every off-diagonal entry is -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m rho)) <= 0 for 0 <= rho < 1; sympy confirms the off-diagonal and diagonal formulas with zero residual for m = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7. (2) For f proportional to exp(-z^T Q z/2): log f(u)+log f(v)-log f(x)-log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j) because the diagonal terms cancel (u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2); the bracket is 0 when x_i - y_i and x_j - y_j have the same sign and (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise, so with Q_ij <= 0 every term is >= 0 and f(x v y) f(x ^ y) >= f(x) f(y): MTP2. Numerically, 4,000 random pairs at each of rho = 0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95 (m = 6): minimum margin -1.4e-14 (zero up to rounding); negative control rho = -0.15 violates the inequality in 3,879 of 4,000 pairs, so the sign condition is what matters. (3) One-sided p_i = 1 - Phi(z_i) is decreasing in each coordinate: a decreasing map in every coordinate swaps join and meet, so f(-x) is MTP2 whenever f is, and an increasing coordinatewise map with Jacobian a product of one-coordinate factors leaves the inequality unchanged because {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i}; I also checked the p-value-scale density directly (3 rho values, 3,000 pairs each): minimum margin -4.4e-15. (4) Subvectors of an MTP2 vector are MTP2, so the 450 true-null statistics of Lab 5 (m_0 = 450) are MTP2 whatever the 50 false-null means. (5) Simes: LR Theorem 3.2(ii) needs P(union_{l <= m_0} {q_(l) <= l alpha/m_0}) <= alpha; Theorem 7.5's event is the union over l <= M = min(floor(gamma m)+1, m_0) <= m_0, a subset, so P(FDP > gamma) <= alpha. Monte Carlo of the Simes event for m_0 = 450 and alpha = 0.05 (20,000 replications each): 0.0502, 0.0231, 0.0169, 0.0260, 0.0322 at rho = 0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95, 0.99, all at or below 0.05 within the standard error (0.0015 at rho = 0, where Simes is exact), and consistent with Lab 5's printed exceedance of the uncorrected constants (at most 0.014 at the three rho values). Assumptions are complete on the page (validity of the true-null p-values; MTP2 of their joint law).

rows.evidence: unchanged since 202ea24 (git diff checked); round-11 evidence: Re-resolved this round. Crossref (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1214/009053605000000084, no identifying parameters): 'Generalizations of the familywise error rate', E. L. Lehmann and Joseph P. Romano, The Annals of Statistics 33(3) 1138-1154, issued 2005-06; equals the registry entry (doi 10.1214/009053605000000084, verified_by crossref; `verify_refs.py --offline` -> 549 entries, 0 problems). Abstract read: k-FWER procedures without dependence assumptions; 'Here, we construct methods such that, for any gamma and alpha, P{FDP > gamma} <= alpha. Two stepdown methods are proposed. The first holds under mild conditions on the dependence structure of p-values, while the second is more conservative but holds without any dependence assumptions.' Locator checked in the text: arXiv math/0507420v1 (the IMS-typeset reprint, header 'The Annals of Statistics 2005, Vol. 33, No. 3, 1138-1154'; pdftotext, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify11-L05-L06/lr/lr_arxiv.txt lines 596-660). Theorem 3.2: 'Let q(1) <= ... <= q(|I|) denote the ordered p-values of the true nulls. Set M = min(floor(gamma s)+1, |I|). (i) For the stepdown procedure with alpha_i given by (26), P{FDP > gamma} <= P{union_{i<=M} {q(i) <= i alpha/|I|}}. (ii) Therefore, if the joint distribution of the p-values of the true null hypotheses satisfies Simes inequality, that is P{q(1) <= alpha/|I| or q(2) <= 2 alpha/|I| or ... or q(|I|) <= alpha} <= alpha, then P{FDP > gamma} <= alpha.' Then, after the proof: 'In fact, there are many joint distributions of positively dependent variables for which Simes inequality is known to hold. In particular, Sarkar and Chang [11] and Sarkar [10] have shown that the Simes inequality holds for the family of distributions which is characterized by the multivariate positive of order 2 condition, as well as some other important distributions.' That is exactly what the card says ('MTP2 implies the Simes inequality (Sarkar; Sarkar and Chang, as Lehmann and Romano note after Theorem 3.2)'), with Theorem 3.2(ii) for the consequence. Attribution and scope: the remark is about distributions of p-values, here the true-null p-values; the card applies it to one-sided p-values of equicorrelated normals, which are MTP2 (L05-math-card-c180). References [10] and [11] of the paper re-resolved by Crossref: Sarkar (1998), Ann. Statist. 26(2) 494-504, doi 10.1214/aos/1028144846, abstract 'Some new probability inequalities involving the ordered components of an MTP2 random vector are derived, which provide an analytical proof of an important conjecture in the field of multiple hypothesis testing...'; Sarkar and Chang (1997), JASA 92(440) 1601-1608, doi 10.1080/01621459.1997.10473682, 'The Simes Method for Multiple Hypothesis Testing with Positively Dependent Test Statistics': both titles match Lehmann and Romano's attribution. Published version: Project Euclid and doi.org returned a bot-challenge page (HTTP 200, 1.2 kB) to my requests, so I could not open the typeset article; the arXiv copy carries the journal's own header and numbering (Theorem 3.2, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.3) matching every locator the lesson uses, and I cannot rule out a wording difference in the final article. Freshness and counter-evidence: no newer version of a 2005 journal article; a Crossref search for 2023 onward ('Simes inequality MTP2 positive dependence false discovery exceedance', journal articles, 12 rows) found no published result that contradicts the Simes inequality under MTP2; the only close hits (Royen 2026, Finner and Roters 2024) are about MTP2 inequalities for other statistics and have no deposited abstract. Sarkar (1998) and Sarkar and Chang (1997) are not in the registry, so the card cannot cite them directly; it names them only through Lehmann and Romano's note, as the lesson does (registry flag kept).

rows.evidence: Checked at 38e33ad, L05.html line 1163 (problem R3 solution, comparison paragraph): 'The streamlined algorithm adds back only the k-1 least significant rejections; it rejects at least as much as the generic one and is justified asymptotically, but it would not control the k-FWER in finite samples with exact critical values.' Romano and Wolf (2007, dl/fulltext/rw_clean.txt) state only that 'control of the k-FWER is also achieved by the computationally less expensive streamlined Algorithm 2.2' in the setting of their Theorem 3.1, which is asymptotic. Their finite-sample remark concerns the theory applying to 'exact finite sample control in certain situations'; it does not say the streamlined algorithm fails in finite samples. The page gives no proof or counterexample for the negative clause, so the sentence is an unsourced claim (BUILDER_RULES 1.2 and 3). The comparison 'e_j >= d_j, so the shortcut is the more conservative' is consistent with the definitions at lines 1158-1162 and was checked.
